versions.note: runtime_by_slot / service_version_by_slot / image_digests are read off the running containers; library and infrastructure-image pins are not recorded here -- they are resolved by identity.git_sha against the build files and infra/compose.yaml

capacity_gate.pg_capacity_projection_basis: no scaling applied: pg_cores unchanged at 3, so the projection equals the measured knee
capacity_gate.projected_knee_basis: PLANNING PROXY, not a measurement: ladder_start_rps 500 x 8 = 4000.0 rps of expected mixed-workload knee. The knee this run actually measures is not known until the first cell's fit, which is what the capacity re-gate (phase `capacity_regate`) tests against

regate.detail: PostgreSQL ran at 0.2524 of its 3-core budget over the first cell's operating-point windows (dotnet is the binding slot), within the 0.7692 ceiling that leaves 1.3x headroom
regate.rule: PostgreSQL cgroup cpu.stat delta / (pg cores x window wall seconds), per slot, over the first cell's operating-point windows; the MAX over slots must be <= 1/headroom_factor. A direct measurement under the actual cells, not a second projection: see capacity_gate.regate_decision
regate.pg_cores_source: cpuset.cpus.effective, read off the measured windows
regate.window_selection: PG UTILIZATION ONLY: confirm-stage windows at each slot's OWN declared confirm rate (`confirm_rates_by_slot`); the common-rate windows the paired verdict uses sit below the operating point and are excluded. This does NOT describe `measured_cache_hit_rate`, which is taken over ALL of the cell's confirm windows (a hit rate is a property of the workload's key draw, not of the rate it was drawn at) -- `cache_hit_rate_source` states its own window count
regate.cache_hit_rate_source: MEASURED: redis INFO keyspace deltas over 6 confirm window(s) of headline.mixed.gc-default

effective_workload.note: spec/ is frozen; the levers produce this effective workload in run state only. Any difference between spec_* and effective_* was APPLIED to the measured cells.

working_set.draw_seed_formula: PCG64(seed=workload.rng.target_generator_seed_default, inc=util.pcg64.stream_for(seed, run_id, cell_id, stage, rate, block, phase))
working_set.note: per-probe draw over 28 measured windows; every attack (each warmup segment, the head-of-window discard, the measured window) draws its own PCG64 stream, so no attack replays another's SEQUENCE. That is not the same as no pre-warming: two independent Zipf draws over one keyspace share the head by construction, and prewarm_containment_per_probe is the measured request-weighted share of each window's reads that an earlier attack had already touched. Counts are the ids the READ path asks for; the write path additionally inserts invoice ids that appear in no target. Create bodies are drawn uniformly from a pool of 150000 built from Zipf customer draws, so the create path's customer_id distribution is that pool's empirical sample rather than a fresh draw per request -- identical on the head, thinner in the tail. The read path is URL-only and unaffected

topology.note: cpuset.cpus.effective / memory.max / memory.swap.max read off each sampled cgroup at window start; the LAST window's values, with the cpuset the compose overlay asked for beside them. swap_current_max_bytes is the OUTCOME: the largest memory.swap.current seen at any window edge, over ALL windows, and swap_peak_max_bytes is the kernel's own high-water mark beside it, which is what catches a cgroup that swapped out and faulted back between two edges
